notes.raw: Exploratory arm, post hoc interval; d > 0 means the Haiku-max try scored higher.

notes.printed: In those two stamped notes, a "try" is a sample, an "arm" is a setting and "at the same money" is cost-matched.

Samples per Haiku-max sample: one Haiku-max sample's list cost divided by the list cost of one sample of the setting in the row. Cost-matched: the vote's k is the floor of the samples per Haiku-max sample, held to the setting's designed samples, so the vote costs no more than one Haiku-max sample. Study 1 costs are in US dollars per puzzle and Study 1b costs in US dollars per answer, as each study stamps them.
On pieces (6×1) the chains' cost-matched vote, k =
4, costs more than one Haiku-max sample (cost column), so it is shown without a paired interval; the cost-matched vote on this shape has k =
Format compliance (pre-specified descriptive) is that of the setting's own samples; a vote is taken over the same samples. Haiku-max was an exploratory setting in Study 1.
No row is a test: the paired differences carry no p-value, no Holm correction and no verdict. Each row stays within one study.
